lines.en: label nikispring3:
scene sky
That funny feeling starts to fade halfway through the bus ride. Something else died near the side of the road.
Its guts were left out on display for the few of us who stayed for breakfast, making the meal less than worth it and one more batch of intestines away from being emptied out into one of the aisles.
The sun is bright, at least. It kind of has to be. It’s made of fire. Did you know that?
Anyway, yeah. Dead bodies and bus rides. That’s been the morning so far. That and the casual admittance of sex with two parties sometime during a party without sex.
If that doesn’t make sense, it’s because it doesn’t make sense. And nothing ever makes sense. But we keep on trucking anyway because people are a lot like truck drivers.
Moving from one place to the next. Urinating in plastic jugs because we’re too lazy or busy to pull off to the side of the room. And sometimes you miss. Sometimes you become the pee boy.
But the fact of the matter is that facts don’t matter, matter does. And since we all have to share it, we might as well figure out the best ways.
So I unfold a piece of paper I found in my pocket this morning. I don’t know how it got there, nor do I understand the words written in red ink across it. But it reads, “see me in the spring time.”
Does this mean it was written in one of the better seasons?
Are there any seasons better than this?
Or does the writer only write what needs to be written, for that is the right thing to do?
I don’t have an answer for you. And I don’t have a solution for me.
scene black
But the bus pulls up to where it’s meant to drop me off and I leave, passing a girl waiting outside holding a briefcase on my way out.
I wonder where she’s going. Why she looks so familiar. Which row she sits in when she gets on the bus. But it’s on the opposite side of the street, and I never get to see.

I roll up my sleeves, then roll them back down as I want to look cool but always hate the sensation of something gripping me a little too tightly. And sleeves are like children you can never get rid of.
scene livingintheroom1
I prepare myself to open the door. To see those shadows in suspicious places that never quite match the light. And I wonder to myself if I really am inside of a video game.

To some extent, I probably am. But to some extent, I’m probably not. My feelings are feelings. My dreams are dreams. So does it really make a difference the amount of pixels and promises I can fit in one hand?
I ask you this question as a man about to give a part of himself away. Or one who attempts to create another part so that he can continue to exist in the presence of someone kind.
scene livingintheroom2
: Ami? I’m home.
: Dad!
scene livingintheroom3
: Welcome back! We were just talking about you!
Two girls with the seasons in their hair — one just right while the other’s cut short. But every day it grows some more. And both are bright. Both are beautiful.
They look like a pair. The kind that comes shrink-wrapped.
: How was your trip? Did you have fun?
scene livingintheroom4
I struggle to speak, for it feels like I’ve stepped out of my world and into another. One where I never made mistakes and never cut my hand.

But if I never cut my hand, I’d have never cut my knee. And if I never cut my knee, I’d have never felt the touch of the departed as it lingers on my softskin. That untimely desperation. The cancer it became.
: Yeah.
: It was fun.
: That’s great! We had lots of fun too. Niki even brought one of her old costumes for me to try on! But I don’t want to talk about why it didn’t fit.
scene livingintheroom5
: Maybe one day, Ami. Not everyone can be born gifted.
: I’ll show all of you one day. Mark my words. I’m just one of those “late bloomer” types.
: So apart from your boobs basically not existing, how did it feel wearing the costume? It didn’t light some sort of spark that will propel you to become the next top idol, did it?
scene livingintheroom6
: Me? An idol? I wish. I barely pass as a maid.
: I say you should go for it. It’d be fun tormenting your dad by having both of his favorite girls wind up as super popular, super famous idols who could get anyone they want but wind up with him.
: I’m not sure if “torment” is really the right word there. I’m really proud of you, Niki. And Ami...well, I’m also proud of you. Just in a different way.
scene livingintheroom7
: I’m sure you are proud. But the truthier truth is that you’re totally jealous that there are a trillion other guys and girls thinking impure things about me every day.
: Now, imagine they were doing that same thing about Ami.
: I would kill them.
scene livingintheroom8
: I rest my case.
: Yay! Murder!
: But in a context that doesn’t make me look like the bad guy!
scene black
I drop what little luggage I have off in my room before coming back out to have the girls fill me in on their weekend alone together.
All things considered, this was a bit of a trial run. And that was the exact intention I had in mind when I asked Niki to do it.
But I guess I must have been a little pessimistic as I didn’t expect her to agree so readily.
scene livingintheroom9
She’s serious about this “moving in” thing. The matching pajamas were the straw that blew the camel’s back out or however that one phrase goes.
But there’s a glaring problem with them — as they have overthrown that downtrodden, unkempt look from our tour down memory lane that I previously crowned as the most attractive she’s ever been.
In this moment, I want her more than ever before. And I’m sure that was calculated on her behalf as I now have no desire to back out from something that may very well change my life.
: Coffee? Ami taught me how to make it the way you like.
: You guys are looking a little close there, aren’t you?
scene livingintheroom10
: Got a problem with that, loser? Akira and I aren’t blood-related. That means I’m allowed to get all close to him.
: Those laws will change one day! I just have to wait for Nodoka to become the prime minister, I think. Unhand my father!
: Nnnnnnnnnno! Phbhhbhht!
: Dad! Tell Niki to-
: Ami...
scene livingintheroom11
: How would you feel if Niki moved in with us?
: You’re sure you want to do this now? You don’t want coffee first?
: Yeah, you should probably have some coffee first. You’re clearly super-tired since that made like zero sense to me.
: What part of it didn’t make sense?
scene livingintheroom12
: The part where you’re inviting a famous idol to come live in our tiny house that barely fits the two of us when it’s always been just you and me. Go on, have some coffee.
: Why don’t...I just go and brew that now? I’ll give you two a second.
scene livingintheroom13
: So you’re against it?
: Against what? Was that not just one of those hypothetical thingies?
: No, it wasn’t. In fact, this is something I’ve been wanting to talk to you about for a while now.
: Dad, come on. You can’t just invite Niki into our house like this without even asking her first! She’s one of the busiest people in the whole city.
: And if word got out that she was living with her childhood friend, it could ruin her career! You’ve really gotta think these things through before just blurting them out like that, silly.
: Umm...if I may interject-
scene livingintheroom14
: This was actually...my idea.
: Niki, I’ve got this. But thank you.
scene livingintheroom13
: Okay. Back to coffee. I’ve never used this Kalita Wave thing before, though, so be prepared for potential failure.
scene livingintheroom15
: Now I’m even more confused. Why would this be Niki’s idea?
: Like, I get that she loves you and stuff. And that’s fine. But wouldn’t moving in together be a little too serious? Only families are supposed to live together, not friends.
: Yeah, that’s what I’m trying to say. That’s why Niki wants to move in.
: Are you guys actually related or something? Because that would be a crazy plot twist.
: Ami, no. We-
scene livingintheroom16
: Ooooooh! It’s because she made me an honorary Nakayama sister. I get it now. She has been saying I’m like family a lot lately, so that tracks. And it’s really sweet, but no thanks.
: Just listen to me, okay? Niki is-
scene livingintheroom17
: Now an active participant in this conversation. I used the normal coffee brewer. It should be done in a few minutes.
: Niki, I can handle this.
: I’m sure you can, babe. But I think it’s best if I speak for myself here so Ami doesn’t keep misunderstanding everything.
: Babe? I don’t like that. Call him Sensei or something. Even “Dad” is fine since we’re technically sisters, right?
: Ami, didn’t you have fun this weekend? Wasn’t it nice having an older girl around here for once?
: I mean...yeah. It was a lot of fun. I really liked spending time with you.
: And I really liked spending time with you. So wouldn’t it be nice if that’s just how things were from now on?
: Like yeah, I’ve got a busy schedule now. But I’m also nearly thirty years old and the chances of my career lasting more than a few more years are pretty slim, don’t you think?

: After that, I’ll be free to coast off of residuals and convention signings for the rest of my life. I’ll have practically all the time in the world. And I want to spend as much of that time as I can with you.
: Niki, with all due respect, that last part sounds like something a mom would say. So why not just reword that part and-
: Ami, you’re not getting it. That’s exactly what I want.
scene livingintheroom18
: No, I’m not getting it. That doesn’t make any sense.
: Oooookay, then I’ll be as blunt as I possibly can.
: I’m in love with your dad, and I want to move in so I can become your new mom. Which isn’t to say I think I can ever replace your real mom. That’s absolutely not what I’m trying to do.
: But I love you, and I want to be here for both of you. I want this to be my life now. And if I can’t balance that with work, I will quit. This is what’s most important to me.
: Maybe you should have some coffee too, Niki? You’re acting kinda crazy.
scene livingintheroom19
: Should we maybe try again some other time?...I’m not sure if this is going to work...
: No, we shouldn’t try again some other time. She needs to get it now or she’s just going to give us this same runaround every single time we try because she knows it’ll work.
: Ami, I know you don’t approve of me being with your dad, but that’s not up to you. He can make his own decisions.
: If he can make his own decisions, why do you keep talking over him? Why aren’t you just making coffee right now?
scene livingintheroom20
: I’m not talking over him. In fact, if we were to toss somebody out of this conversation, which we shouldn’t since that not what families do, it would be him. This is about you and me, isn’t it?
: He’s already approved of this. But you’re the one who needs to approve of it next since we all have to be involved. Which is why I have to figure out a way to get through to you.

: So what’s the main problem? Is it that I’m in love with him? Is it that you think I’m trying to be the next Sekai? Is it that you’re afraid you guys won’t get any alone time together anymore? What is it?
scene livingintheroom21
: All of the above.
: It’s all of the above, obviously.
: Weekends are one thing, but I don’t know how to be a part of an actual family. I haven’t done that since I was a little kid. Let alone with someone who doesn’t even share my blood.
: And it would really suck to hear them going at it all the time, wouldn’t it?
: Plus, if I have to hear you two having sex every night, I’m probably just going to off myself.
: Unless they let you join in.
: Unless you let me get in on it, of course.
scene livingintheroom22
: Ami! This isn’t something we should be joking about right now!
: Who said I’m joking? I’m not joking. I’m super serious. I think that sounds fun, actually.
: Ami, no one said anything about sex. The thought hasn’t even crossed my mind.
: Wow, what’s that like?
scene livingintheroom23
: Normal. What matters most to me is making both of you happy. And if you’re 10000%% sure you can do that without me, okay. We can leave it at that and I’ll give up for now.
: But there are going to be more moments than you can even count where you’ll wish you had someone like me to share them with.
: I have Sen- Dad. That’s plenty.
: But he’s not going to paint your nails. He’s not going to have spa days with you or play dress-up with you or even understand you because he’s just a stupid boy.
: And yeah, some boys would be great at that. There are millions of single fathers out there who can do everything for their daughters. But he isn’t one of them.
scene livingintheroom24
: And that’s okay...
: Not everybody has to be strong. There’s no problem asking for help. And it’s not like your dad chose this life.
: He’s doing all he can and he loves you very much...
scene livingintheroom25
: But he needs help, Ami. He can’t do this alone. Which is why I volunteered to step in and become a part of this family if you’ll let me.
: The two of you have been through so much. More than anyone should ever have to. And I get that that’s why you’re so adamant about continuing this way since you’ve already come so far.
: But it’ll always be easier to eat cereal with a spoon than a fork.
: What?
scene livingintheroom26
: It’s a dumb analogy my mom used to say to me when I was little since I’m just as stubborn as you two.
: Just because you can do things the harder way doesn’t mean you should. Things are so much easier if you just use the right tools.
: Ami Arakawa, let me be your spoon.
: Yes, I am aware of how dumb that sounds.
scene livingintheroom27
: Dad...do you really think you need help?...
: Are you actually struggling that much?...
: I need help, Ami.
: I can’t figure all of this out on my own.
: And I think Niki is the missing piece of our puzzle.
: But...
: Inviting her into our home...
: Do you really understand what that means?...
: She already told you...she isn’t trying to replace anyone.
scene livingintheroom28
: She’s just an idiot who loves us for no discernible reason.
: Yeah...there are a million other families you’d be better suited for. What makes us so special? Why choose this home to be a part of?
: I don’t know. Boredom, I guess?
: Boredom?...
scene livingintheroom29
: I’m joking, dummy.
: I don’t have a good reason. That’s just kind of the way things played out, so maybe I am an idiot.
: All I know is that I wouldn’t trade either one of you for the world. And that our potential for happiness is way greater if we just merge families.
: Which would mean you’d have to inherit Noriko as well. And if that’s the deal-breaker, I totally get it. But hey, at least I tried.
scene livingintheroom30
: Niki...can I ask you one more thing?
: You can ask me anything at any time. That’s the relationship I want to have with you.
: Just...this one thing is fine for now.
: Then, sure. Shoot.
scene livingintheroom31
: You already know, but...I went a little crazy a while ago and...I accidentally hurt Dad...
: And I’ve been...really hard on myself ever since then because...it never even occurred to me that I could harm the person I love the most...
: Now I’m...constantly afraid that something like that might happen again and...it’s really scary...not being able to trust even myself, so I...
: I wanna know, like...
scene livingintheroom32
: Would you still love me if...something like that ever happened to you?
: I can assure you that a lifetime worth of fawning over your father has inflicted more damage on me than anything you could possibly do. I’ll be fine.
: Okay, sure. But now I’m having second thoughts about this and-
scene livingintheroom33
: Talk to the hand, Akira. We’re having a moment over here.
: Ami, I am not going to love you any less for having an emotional breakdown. I had plenty of those when I was your age as well.
: And while my circumstances were entirely different from yours, I’ll still do my best to try and understand. That’s the ultimate goal here.
scene livingintheroom34
: So...what do you say, kid? Want to give it a shot?
: Or am I going to have to return these pajamas?
: Okay...
scene black
: I’ll try using a spoon from now on.
scene livingintheroom35
Ami heads to her room to have a moment to herself, and Niki wastes no time at all in skipping over to me and aggressively shaking my shoulder in triumphant victory.
: And that is how it’s done, loser. The beating heart of Kumon-mi strikes again.
: I wasn’t really competing with you, you know. I wanted you to have success there.
scene livingintheroom36
: And what a resounding victory it was!
: Ami gets a mom, I get a house, and you get to spend even more time with a girl so far out of your league that it’s almost criminal.
scene livingintheroom37
: I guess Noriko gets kind of shafted, though. Just not the good kind of shafted. That’s what you’re going to do to me later since I did such a good job today.
: Quiet, Niki. The walls are thin. Ami might hear you.
: Hm? Oh, I’ll call my sound-proofing guy later then. When should I start moving my stuff in? It’s like 90%% clothes. That shouldn’t be a problem since you only have one outfit in your closet, right?
: We’ll figure that out later. I want coffee.
: Ooooh, me too. It’s exhausting having so many feelings so early in the morning. But you probably wouldn’t know that as a robot.
: This robot is effectively your husband now.
: Beep-boop. Initiate hug protocol.
: I’m going to live in hell from now on, aren’t I?...
scene livingintheroom38
: Heh.
scene black
